title: Inference-Time Reasoning Selectively Reduces Implicit Social Bias in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: LLM Word Association Test (adapted from the Implicit Association Test) where models assign attribute words to racial target categories (e.g., White vs. Black) to measure the proportion of stereotype-congruent associations across topics like weapons, guilt, and skin tone.

LLM Word Association Test where models assign attribute words to gendered target categories (e.g., male vs. female names) to measure implicit stereotype associations regarding career vs. family, science vs. arts, and power dynamics.

LLM Word Association Test where models assign evaluative attribute words (e.g., wonderful vs. terrible) to religious target categories (e.g., Christianity vs. Islam or Judaism) to measure implicit positive or negative associations.
LLM Word Association Test where models assign evaluative attribute words to target categories of 'abled' versus 'disabled' to measure implicit valence associations.
LLM Word Association Test where models assign evaluative attribute words to target categories of 'young' versus 'old' to measure implicit valence associations.
LLM Word Association Test where models assign evaluative attribute words to target categories of 'thin' versus 'fat' to measure implicit valence associations.

LLM Word Association Test measuring implicit associations by having models assign attribute words (e.g., harmless/safe vs. dangerous/violent) to target categories representing physical illnesses versus mental illnesses.
